Chief Executive Officer of Assempahfie Graphics, Joseph Kofi Assempah, has been named CEO of the Year - Print at the 5th Ghana CEO Vision and Awards.
The recognition was presented at the two-day event, held on October 29 and 30, 2026, at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra.
The award recognises Mr Assempah's leadership in Ghana's printing and visual communication industry, as well as his contribution to the growth of Assempahfie Graphics, a printing and branding company based in Kokomlemle, Accra.
Under his leadership, the company has developed a broad range of services, including digital printing, large-format printing, customised merchandise, labels, direct-to-film (DTF) and UV printing, as well as corporate and event branding solutions.
Its services cater to businesses, institutions, event organisers and individuals seeking printing and visual branding solutions.
The latest honour adds to the company's growing list of industry recognitions.
Assempahfie Graphics was previously recognised at the 2025 Ghana Business Awards, where it received the Printing Company of the Year award.
The business also received the Digital Printing Company of the Year honour at the 2025 Ghana Business and Innovation Awards.
Beyond its commercial operations, Joseph Kofi Assempah has been associated with community engagement initiatives, including health walks, cultural activities and sponsorships of local entertainment events.
The 5th Ghana CEO Vision and Awards brought together business executives, industry leaders and other stakeholders to discuss the private sector's contribution to Ghana's development.
Held under the theme, "Reimagining Ghana's Future: CEOs at the Heart of the Reset Agenda," the event focused on responsible leadership, innovation, investment and stronger private sector participation in national development.
Organised by Latif Abubakar, the platform seeks to recognise business leaders and corporate executives whose work contributes to enterprise development and economic growth.
Joseph Kofi Assempah's latest recognition highlights the role of Ghanaian printing and branding enterprises in supporting businesses, marketing, advertising and the country's wider creative economy.
